rubric.result: The objective promises three things and the diff produces all three in production code. 'An adapter owns terminals': PtyLiveSessions extends LiveSessions, open() spawns through the injected TerminalSpawn and keeps each opened terminal in the private #open map keyed by session id, so all() and find() answer from it and #exited() drops it. 'Keeps each one's scrollback': OpenTerminal carries its own scrollback string, #received() appends every chunk through #trimmed(), and watch() answers that string as printed. 'Fans its bytes out to whoever is watching': each OpenTerminal holds a Set of watchers, #received() iterates it, and stop() removes only the watcher that asked. Nothing the objective names is missing and nothing in the diff is a behaviour it does not name.

The TDD line asks for it('a watcher receives what the terminal printed before it arrived') — 'a doubled spawn emits two chunks, then a watcher arrives and its printed is both chunks joined, in order'. The test at pty-live-sessions.test.ts:182-190 prints 'hello ' then 'world' through the spawn double, only then calls sessions.watch(...), and asserts expect(watch.printed).toBe('hello world'). Same assertion, same input, same expected value, and the order is the one the sentence fixes (the join reads 'hello world', not 'worldhello ').

Compared name by name with the Contract block. Terminal and TerminalSpawn are exported with the same members, parameter names and order (file, argv, options{name, cols, rows, cwd, env}). PtyLiveSessions extends LiveSessions and declares every constant with the literal the brief states: TERM 'xterm-256color', COLUMNS 80, ROWS 24, LOGIN_INTERACTIVE '-il', FALLBACK_SHELL '/bin/sh', SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS 262_144 (the numeric separator leaves the value identical to 262144). The constructor takes exactly {spawn, shell, cwd, env, newId, stderr} with the declared types and open() returns LiveSession. The prose of the block is honoured piece by piece: argv is [LOGIN_INTERACTIVE], the id comes from newId(), the name is the basename of the shell, every onData chunk is appended and trimmed from the front to the last SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS and handed to every watcher, watch() answers the scrollback as printed plus a stop that deletes only that watcher, onExit forgets the session so find() and all() stop naming it, the env drops undefined entries and forces TERM, and there is one stderr line on open and one on exit, each naming the id and the program. all/find/watch/write are the port's own signatures (live-sessions.ts), matched exactly.

Rows the diff bears on: P-1 (the port is synchronous) — every method returns without a promise, including watch(), which is what lets a route write its headers before the first byte. P-6 — <shell> -il, name/TERM 'xterm-256color', 80 columns, 24 rows, the injected cwd, /bin/sh when shell is undefined, and the session named after the basename of the program. P-7 — 262144 characters, oldest dropped first (#trimmed slices from the front), and the scrollback is what a later subscriber receives as printed. P-8 — every identifier, test name and stderr line is English. D-10 — the module and its test are TypeScript with erasable syntax only. P-4 is not reopened: the diff imports no node-pty at all, it takes the spawn by the constructor, so the pin stays a later task's wiring. P-2, P-3, P-5, P-9 and D-1..D-25 have no bearing on this file, and the diff implements nothing against them.

Exemplars: the adapter reads like probed-tool-sessions.ts — extends its port, calls super(), takes every collaborator by name through the constructor, keeps its policy values as static readonly on the class and its work in private methods; the stderr collaborator is the harvest-clock.ts idiom, injected as (line: string) => void, and the test injects stderr: (line) => written.push(line) and asserts the exact lines exactly as harvest-clock.test.ts does. The trailing \n added in the repair matches every other producer in this backend (git-workspace.ts:301, review-watch.ts:166, worktree-plans.ts:119, harvest-clock's lines) against the single sink ct-api.ts:280 `stderr: (line) => process.stderr.write(line)`, which terminates nothing itself. Rules: style.md — no comment or docstring anywhere in the diff, every identifier and message English, and no free function at module level (production is one class; the test's helpers hang off TerminalDouble, SpawnDouble, Ids, Cabin and OpenedTerminal). architecture.md — an infrastructure adapter importing only domain, direction respected; Terminal, TerminalSpawn and OpenTerminal are the boundary model of this adapter and share its file while it is their only consumer, which that document allows by name; backend/conventions/this-repository.md's layout and .ts extension in relative imports are honoured. boundaries.md — 'an adapter is named after its implementation, not after its port' (PtyLiveSessions, not LiveSessionsAdapter); the spawn options are the literal payload node-pty takes, entered by the contract's own names. domain.md — no tool noun leaks into the port or the value object; 'Terminal' is the adapter's word, inside the adapter. decisions.md — the trim rule, the environment rule and the naming rule each live in exactly one place here. simplicity.md's observability rule — the brief names the reader of the two stderr lines ('whoever runs make run-backend can tell a live cabin terminal from a dead one'), so the burden is discharged, and after the repair both lines are watched. testing.md — the adapter is cut right before the external system and the assertion is on the literal request sent (spawn.calls with file, argv and the whole options object); there is no parse of a declared output shape here (the terminal returns raw bytes), so there is no capture whose provenance could be named. defects.md, rule by rule: (1) closed vocabulary — no subject: nothing in this diff classifies anything, there is no dispatch and so no catch-all branch, and find() answers LiveSession | null rather than a boolean derived from a state; (2) raw map as the return value of logic — none: the only maps are the private #open index, never returned, and the env Record that #environmentOf builds as the payload of the spawn call, which is the last step before the external system; watch() returns the port's declared LiveSessionStream, whose fields are read by name and checked by the type checker; (3) two fields that have to agree — none, and no sentinel: the absence of a session is null in the type, the scrollback's empty string genuinely means nothing has been printed rather than standing for a missing value, and the #open key is written from session.id in the single place that inserts; (4) an error named for where — no error type is introduced; the one throw is a plain Error whose message says what happened ('holds no live terminal for session …'). Two tensions declared rather than reported, because the brief's own Contract block fixes them and the implementer could not have written it otherwise: boundaries.md's 'no external system is called without a cap, and the adapter does not choose the cap' has no room in a constructor the contract spells out and would contradict D-1/P-3/P-6, where the session is unbounded by design; and 'an adapter does not decide policy' sits against the contract's instruction to hold TERM, COLUMNS, ROWS and SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS as static readonly on this class. One nit reported as low below. No delivery-shape rule of either yardstick bears on a new file with no call site yet.
Does not apply: both files are new (new file mode 100644) and the diff carries no - line at all, so no pre-existing assertion, case or test was removed, relaxed or rewritten.

Every behaviour the objective promises is produced by backend/src/infrastructure/pty-live-sessions.ts: the scrollback and its trimming (#received/#trimmed), the fan-out and the per-watcher stop (watch/#received), the naming (#basenameOf), the environment (#environmentOf) and the forgetting on exit (#exited). The doubles stand only where the external system is — TerminalDouble and SpawnDouble replace node-pty, which testing.md prescribes for an adapter — and every assertion is on what the adapter did with them (what it sent to spawn, what printed answered, what write reached the terminal, what stderr received). This is exactly where attempt 1's medium lived, and it is closed: the two stderr lines are now pinned as literal strings, so neither the call nor its trailing newline can be deleted and leave the suite green.

The diff writes only the two declared paths, both (create), and nothing else — no plan hunk, so there is no amendment to rule on. Inside them, every line traces to a sentence of the task: the class, its constants and its five methods to the Contract block; each test of the Tests list to its own name; and the two tests that are not in the Tests list — the stderr pair — to the contract sentence 'One stderr line on open and one on exit, each naming the id and the program', which is behaviour this task owes and which nothing else in the file was watching. The trailing \n is part of what makes that a line rather than an addition of its own, given the sink writes the string unchanged. Out of scope is untouched: no endpoint, no route, no node-pty wiring, no resize and nothing that kills a session.

Eleven new tests, all in the new test file. Deterministic: no clock, no date, no network, no filesystem, no sleep and no randomness — the ids come from Ids.sequential(), the cwd is the constant '/repo/cabin' and never touched, and the spawn is a double. Isolated: OpenedTerminal.with() builds a fresh PtyLiveSessions, a fresh spawn double and a fresh id sequence per test, there is no module-level mutable state and no test depends on another's order (every one of them sees 'session-1'). Verifies real behaviour: every assertion is on what the adapter did — the literal argv and options handed to spawn, the printed the adapter composed, the bytes each watcher received, what write() reached the terminal with, what find()/all() answer after an exit, and the exact stderr strings; reverting the production lines of this diff makes each of them fail, which the two new stderr tests now also do. The skill control-tower-loop:test-driven-development loaded, with its testing-anti-patterns.md reference: no assertion checks a mock's existence or call count, no test-only method was added to the production class, the doubles are complete against the Terminal contract this adapter declares, and the mock setup is not the bulk of any test. Three prescribed names carry an 'and' where the skill asks for one behaviour per test ('a stopped watcher receives nothing more and the session stays live', 'the scrollback keeps the last 262144 characters and drops the oldest', 'the shell is the login interactive one, and /bin/sh when SHELL is unset'), but all three are verbatim from the plan's Tests list, so the implementer could not split them without deviating from the task — declared here rather than reported, and the two tests the implementer chose himself are single-behaviour. Assertions over the policy constants (TERM, COLUMNS, ROWS, SCROLLBACK_CHARACTERS) are written against the constants rather than their literals, which testing.md's 'what stays unmeasured, on purpose' licenses: the mechanism is measured (the at-limit case drops nothing, the limit-plus-one case drops exactly the first character and keeps the length at the limit), the numbers are the recorded decision.

findings.what: The basename is hand-rolled in a private static instead of taken from node:path, which this backend already imports in five modules (ct-api.ts:6 uses dirname and join, git-workspace.ts:1 isAbsolute). conventions/simplicity.md puts the burden of proof on what is added, and four added lines that the platform already answers do not discharge it; path.basename would also be right about the edges this version is not (a trailing slash yields '', which LiveSession then refuses). Nothing observable changes for the shells this task spawns, hence low.
